lessons.title: Reading tables
lessons.subtitle: Week 11: Data and everyday decisions
lessons.body:
A table has rows and columns with defined meanings. Check headings, units, and missing values before calculating or drawing conclusions.

Offline practice: Create a fictional table of weekly study minutes and explain each column. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A table has rows and columns with defined meanings. Check headings, units, and missing values before calculating or drawing conclusions.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Averages and variation
lessons.subtitle: Week 11: Data and everyday decisions
lessons.body:
An average summarises data but can hide differences. Compare individual values and extreme observations before describing a typical experience.

lessons.title: Missing and incorrect data
lessons.subtitle: Week 11: Data and everyday decisions
lessons.body:
Missing data is not automatically zero. Incorrect entries and duplicates can distort results; corrections should have an explanation.

Offline practice: Inspect a fictional attendance table with one blank and one duplicate and record your decisions. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

lessons.title: Evaluation measures
lessons.subtitle: Week 11: Data and everyday decisions
lessons.body:
Accuracy counts the proportion of correct classifications but can be misleading with uneven categories. Inspect mistakes and the purpose of the task as well.

Offline practice: Explain why predicting not spam for every message looks accurate when only one of one hundred messages is spam. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

lessons.title: An evidence-based recommendation
lessons.subtitle: Week 11: Data and everyday decisions
lessons.body:
A recommendation should show its evidence, assumptions, limitations, and alternatives. Data can inform a choice without making the choice automatically.

Offline practice: Write a fictional recommendation for study-session timing using a small table and a limitation statement. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A recommendation should show its evidence, assumptions, limitations, and alternatives. Data can inform a choice without making the choice automatically.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
